Top up-regulated proteins and their pathway network

Source: R/plot_pathway_network.R
plot_pathway_network.Rd

Reproduces the classic "Top Up-regulated Pathways" figure: a horizontal bar chart (left) counting the number of pathways per up-regulated protein, with the fold-change printed to the left of each bar, combined side-by-side with a bipartite gene-pathway network (right) drawn with `ggraph`. Genes are coloured by fold change; pathway nodes are grey and labelled.

Usage

plot_pathway_network(
  de_table,
  pathway_map = NULL,
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  top_n = 12,
  palette = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

de_table

A data.frame of differential-expression results with an assay/protein column and a numeric fold-change column (long format).

pathway_map

Optional assay->pathway mapping. Either a data.frame with assay and pathway columns, or a named list where each name is a pathway and the value is a character vector of assays belonging to it. If NULL, the first `Pathway`/`Panel` column of `de_table` is used as the mapping.

assay_col

Name of the assay/protein column. If NULL, auto-detected.

value_col

Name of the numeric fold-change column (e.g. "log2FC" or "estimate"). If NULL, auto-detected from common names.

top_n

Number of top up-regulated proteins to include (default 12).

palette

Optional themed palette for the fold-change gradient: a palette name from `olinkviz_palettes()` or a character vector of hex colors. If NULL (default), the classic reference colours are used.

title

Plot title (annotation over both panels).

seed

Random seed for the reproducible network layout (default 123).

Value

A `patchwork` object combining the bar chart and the network.

Details

The network is a bipartite graph connecting each up-regulated protein to the pathways it belongs to (supplied via `pathway_map`). Use the `palette` argument to colour both panels with one of the OlinkViz themed palettes (`olinkviz_palettes()`); by default the classic reference colours are used (red bars, blue->green->yellow->red fold-change gradient, grey pathways).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot_pathway_network(bansal_univariate, value_col = "estimate",
                     palette = "jewel", top_n = 12)
} # }
